critic.reading: 15,800 is a rate scaling, not a cost computation, and exceeds both cost-based figures in the corpus
critic.holds: eq. (3) is eq. (2.2) x 125, a mutation-rate ratio; Haldane over the same window gives 1,500 (675 with d), so 15,800 is 10.5x Haldane, 32x the 487 and 2.4x Term 3's ~6,650

notes: The arithmetic of the chain holds within rounding: 126.6 (127), 15,820 (15,800; 15,875 from the rounded 127), 10.3 million (10 million). No step links eq. (3) to the cost of selection: the factor 125 is a mutation-rate ratio, and a cost-based count over 450,000 generations is 1,500 at 1/300 (675 with d). 'Perhaps more in line with equation (3)' therefore has no derivation; at 0.035 per generation it would need about one selected fixation per 28 generations. H5's derived line cites Term 3 as 'about 6,690', while H1 and H8 give 6,650; M-808 asserts the closed form 6,652 (6,690 is the rounded 8.3e-12).
